# The static saved-layout and topology helpers accept a reserved name

Leaf of #18605 (parent linked natively; blocked by #18609, whose reservation rule this leaf extends to the static write paths). `Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0029 (as amended by #18606: the §2.2 selection contract)`.

`unowned-rationale:` filed from the author seat of #18627 during its review round; small, engine-only, claimable by self-selection once #18609 merges.

## Context

Surfaced by @neo-gpt-emmy's #18627 review intake: the dock example (#18610 / PR #18631) keeps a plain collection through the static `PerspectiveLibrary` helpers, so the instance-only reservation rule never reaches it. Measured at the #18609 head (78c18c637a) in the Node unit runtime: `PerspectiveLibrary.upsertSavedLayout(collection, layout)` with `layoutId: '$default'` returns no error and stores the record under `$default`; `Persistence.createTopologyCollection([topology])` with a `$default` topology returns no error and lists it; the instance `savePerspective` of the same layout refuses with `"$default" is an engine-reserved perspective name` and, with `declaredPerspectives` wired, `"review" names a declared perspective`.

## The Problem

#18609 places the reservation rule — a saved record may equal a declared perspective but never define or impersonate one; `$`-prefixed names are engine-reserved — at the instance libraries' write boundary: `PerspectiveLibrary#savePerspective` / `#renamePerspective` and `TopologyLibrary#save` call `Persistence.reservedNameErrors(keys, declaredPerspectives)`. The static collection helpers are a second write boundary the rule never reaches. A consumer that keeps a plain collection (built through `createSavedLayoutCollection`, read through `restoreActiveSavedLayout`, mutated through `upsertSavedLayout`) and the Neural Link's topology capture (`DockService.storeTopology` → `Persistence.createTopologyCollection`) can both write a record named `$default` — the zones-only workspace's one declared name. Once #18613 lands, `restore_perspective('$default')` on such a holder meets the ambiguous-name refusal against the declared list, and the declared perspective is shadowed by a stored record it can never define.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Persistence.RESERVED_NAME_PREFIX` + `Persistence.reservedNameErrors(keys, declared)` (`src/dashboard/dock/model/Persistence.mjs:110–120` at 78c18c637a): the prefix refusal needs no declared set; the declared-name refusal needs the consumer's `declaredPerspectives` wiring and is instance-only by design — the engine never instantiates a library.
- `PerspectiveLibrary.upsertSavedLayout` (`src/dashboard/dock/persistence/PerspectiveLibrary.mjs:271`): validates the collection and the record (`Persistence.restoreSavedLayout`), then stores under `layoutId` — no name rule. The instance `savePerspective` (`:525–545`) runs `UNSAFE_KEYS`, then `reservedNameErrors`, then its collision logic.
- `Persistence.createTopologyCollection` (`model/Persistence.mjs:833`) validates through `validateTopologyCollection` (`:732`) — schema and id checks, no name rule; `DockService.storeTopology` (`src/ai/client/DockService.mjs:118`) builds every Neural Link topology capture through it.

## The Fix

- The prefix rule goes into the two collection **validators** — `PerspectiveLibrary.validateSavedLayoutCollection` and `Persistence.validateTopologyCollection` — as `Persistence.reservedNameErrors([layoutId, perspectiveName])` over every contained record: that covers the three static writers (`createSavedLayoutCollection`, `upsertSavedLayout`, `createTopologyCollection`, and `DockService.storeTopology` through the last) and every borrowed read symmetrically, in one implementation. Intake finding by @neo-gpt-emmy: `createSavedLayoutCollection` installs arbitrary records directly, so an upsert-only refusal would leave the same hole at the factory.
- Raw individual layout / topology capture stays valid: the collection namespace is where a name becomes addressable.
- The instance `savePerspective` / `renamePerspective` / `TopologyLibrary#save` keep the declared-set check and reuse the same helper (the declared-name refusal stays instance-only — a static helper cannot know the declared set); the docblocks say which rule applies where.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PerspectiveLibrary.validateSavedLayoutCollection` — and through it `createSavedLayoutCollection`, `upsertSavedLayout` and every borrowed read | #18609's reservation rule (`Persistence.RESERVED_NAME_PREFIX`) | a `$`-prefixed `layoutId` or `perspectiveName` in any contained record is a validation error (`"<key>" is an engine-reserved perspective name`); factory and upsert return the collection unchanged with that error | — | docblocks | unit arms: `$default` refused at the factory and at upsert, `default` stored |
| `Persistence.validateTopologyCollection` — and through it `createTopologyCollection` and `DockService.storeTopology` | same | a `$`-prefixed topology id or name in any contained record is a validation error | — | docblocks | unit arms: a `$default` topology refused at the factory; the Neural Link topology capture reports `saved: false` with the error |
| instance `savePerspective` / `renamePerspective` / `TopologyLibrary#save` | unchanged | the declared-name refusal through `declaredPerspectives` stays here | — | — | #18609's arms stay green |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `validateSavedLayoutCollection` refuses a `$`-prefixed `layoutId` and `perspectiveName` in any contained record with the instance path's error shape, so `createSavedLayoutCollection` and `upsertSavedLayout` refuse and a borrowed collection carrying one fails validation; a plain name still stores.
- [ ] `validateTopologyCollection` refuses a `$`-prefixed topology id or name, so `createTopologyCollection` refuses and `DockService.storeTopology` reports the refusal (`saved: false`, errors) instead of storing.
- [ ] Raw `capturePerspective` / `captureTopologyPerspective` output stays valid regardless of name (the collection namespace is the boundary).
- [ ] #18609's seven arms stay green; the PR `Refs #18605` and `Resolves` this leaf only.

## Out of Scope

Declared-name refusal in the static helpers (needs the consumer's declared set — instance-only by design); the dock example's own save path (it builds its collection from static definitions and saves no user-named record today).
